lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: PJM's 2026/27 capacity price of $329.17/MW-day replaced 2025/26's $269.92 from 2026-06-01, so Q3 2026 is the first full quarter at the higher price (+22%). PSEG clears about 3,600 MW of nuclear in PJM (Q2 call), so the step-up is worth roughly $59/MW-day x ~3,500 MW x 92 days = ~$19m pre-tax, ~$0.03/share against a $1.22 bar. It sits inside the reaffirmed $4.28-4.40 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Power & Other rose to $83m from $52m on higher realized prices and nuclear output, and the total beat was $0.06; the stock fell 0.46% (baseline 2026-08-04). Q3 2025 beat on higher power pricing and rose 0.99%.

findings.finding: NRC daily status reports put PSEG's nuclear units at or near full power through Q3, with no refuelling outage at a PSEG-operated unit. On 2026-07-15 Salem 1, Salem 2, Hope Creek and Peach Bottom 2/3 were all at 100%. On 2026-08-15 Hope Creek was at 88% (a feedwater pump out of service) and Salem was at 100%. On 2026-09-15 Hope Creek was at 98% (condenser leakage), Salem at 100%, and Peach Bottom 2 in coastdown to refuelling. This is against a Q2 capacity factor of 92.0% (93.7% YTD) and a Hope Creek forced outage from Feb to Apr 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nuclear output was cited as a driver of the Q2 2026 Power beat; the stock fell 0.46%. Output beats have not been paid on this name.

findings.finding: Summer 2026 was extreme in PJM: an all-time peak load on 2026-07-02 (~166-168 GW), real-time prices averaging $348/MWh over July 1-3 against a $64 YTD average, and a PSE&G system peak of 10,446 MW, the highest since 2012. Utility peers that have already reported beat: AEP adj. EPS $2.23 vs $2.05 expected; FirstEnergy core $0.98 vs $0.83 a year ago, guide reaffirmed; Exelon $0.87, range narrowed to $2.85-2.91. PSE&G is largely decoupled through its CIP, and Power is mostly hedged (Q2 carried a $258m pre-tax MTM loss on forward positions), so transmission to PSEG is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 'beat on higher power pricing' rose 0.99% (baseline 2025-11-03). The other six prints fell 0.14% to 2.19%.

findings.finding: The early-July 2026 storms were, per the company, 'one of the largest restoration efforts in its history': ~380,000 customers, 330+ crews, 7,000+ A/C repairs. The cost and whether it is expensed or deferred were not disclosed on the Q2 call. Any expensed portion lands as Q3 O&M. Management knew of it on 2026-08-04 and still reaffirmed guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior storm-cost surprise found in the baseline's 7 prints.

findings.finding: Q3 is when PSEG has narrowed or raised the year before: Q3 2025 brought an 'upgraded outlook' and was the only up reaction in 7 prints (+0.99%). In 2026, H1 operating EPS of $2.41 is +9.5% on $2.20, against a guide midpoint of $4.34 that implies +7% on 2025's $4.05. Holding the midpoint needs only H2 of $1.93 (+4% on H2 2025's $1.85). findings.finding: PSE&G said it 'anticipates filing by year-end 2026 to update base rates', years ahead of its 2029 requirement. NJ legislation also removes the 50bp RTO transmission adder from January 2027 (~$40m net income a year, ~$0.08/share). Both are into Governor Sherrill's affordability agenda: a January 2026 executive order on rate freezes and bill credits, and PSE&G bills described by Jefferies as the highest in NJ. Rate-case size, ROE ask or timing given on the call could revive political-risk selling.

The NJ unit is Salem: PSEG operates it and owns 57%, and the NRC list shows PSEG planning stretch-uprate applications for Salem 1 & 2 in Q2 2027. Canary Media puts Salem's uprate at 97 MW. Whether PSEG's 57% share is contracted, and on what terms, has not been disclosed. Its first chance to speak is the Q3 call, where at Q2 it cited 'the potential to contract our nuclear output under multi-year agreements'.
